cands.name: Mike Colvin
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 42 since January 2025. Licensed funeral service professional at Colvin Funeral Homes and Paye Memorial Funeral Establishment, and a political advisor and strategist. Duke University graduate, born in Fayetteville. Former chair of the NC Democratic Party's 8th Congressional District.

endorsements.text: His campaign site says he has the endorsement of his predecessor, retired NC Rep. Marvin Lucas, along with unnamed current and former legislators and elected officials. This is the campaign's own claim.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Colvin grew up, or when or whether he lived outside North Carolina apart from attending Duke. We found no news coverage, interviews or questionnaire answers on his positions, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no stated positions or official actions on data centers, development and land use, homestead taxes, foreign or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or abortion. His campaign site names healthcare, education, economic development, public safety and veterans as priorities, in general terms only. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored did not display, so we cannot say what legislation he carried. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. His endorsements come only from his own campaign site, and Ballotpedia lists none.

local.label: Roots 40: Born in Fayetteville, and his campaign site says he has worked as a licensed funeral service professional in the community for over 20 years; where he grew up is not stated.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2025. Works as a licensed funeral service professional in leadership roles at two funeral homes, and has been a political advisor, strategist and policy advisor to elected officials. Formerly chaired the NC Democratic Party's 8th Congressional District.
qual.why: He has held a legislative seat for one term and has business management and policy-advisory experience. The score is below the top of the range because his legislative tenure is short and he has no law or budget career.
